```markdown
[Date]

Cigna
Appeals Unit
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination — request for reconsideration**

- **Member:** Morgan Ellison
- **Member ID:** W921829662
- **Reference number:** POC-892F80BC2E-98290
- **Date of denial notice:** August 21, 2026
- **Service denied:** Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
- **Requesting surgeon:** Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery
- **Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026 (https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-313%20Hip%20Replace%20Arthro_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf)

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my total hip replacement (CPT 27130), which Cigna denied on August 21, 2026 on the grounds that the procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Cigna to reconsider that decision. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this surgery is needed, and when I compare my records to the plan's own published criteria in Cigna CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026, the records line up with what the policy asks for. Below I set the plan's language next to what is in my chart.

## The plan's criteria and what my records show

**1. Imaging findings.** The policy states:

> "Imaging shows ANY of the following findings:"

and among the findings it lists:

> "Tönnis Grade 2-3 osteoarthritis"

> "avascular necrosis with collapse of the femoral head"

> "inflammatory arthritis affecting BOTH the femoral head and the acetabulum with joint space narrowing"

My weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph dated June 29, 2026 shows joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes. My records report those findings; they do not assign a numeric grade to them. Because this is a criterion that asks for **any** one of several imaging findings, I am asking the reviewer to read the radiograph report itself against the list, and to tell me in writing which imaging finding Cigna concluded was absent.

**2. Symptoms.** The policy states:

> "Symptoms include BOTH of the following:"

The first is:

> "function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two [2] city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration"

My records document 12 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest, and that I walk with a cane and am limited to one block. One block is shorter than the two city blocks the policy gives as its own example of function-limiting distance, and twelve months is well beyond the three months the policy asks for.

The second is:

> "loss of hip function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment"

My records document that I cannot put on my shoes unassisted, that I need a cane to walk, and that my range of motion on exam is limited by pain with positive provocative testing on the affected side. Dressing myself and walking are ordinary daily activities, and my chart shows both are affected.

**3. Failure of non-surgical management.** The policy states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration"

My records document:

- Supervised physical therapy directed at hip abductor strengthening and gait, 24 visits over 10 weeks from April 22, 2026 to July 1, 2026, with a physical therapy discharge note;
- NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief — twice the duration the policy names;
- A corticosteroid injection on May 13, 2026 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.

Taken together, this is provider-directed, non-surgical treatment well beyond three months, and the record shows it failed to control my symptoms.

The policy also contains two exceptions, which I note in case they are relevant to how my case was read:

> "Criteria exception: Three (3) months of function-limiting pain is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider-directed non-surgical management is inappropriate."

> "Criteria exception: Three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider-directed non-surgical management is inappropriate."

I do not need to rely on either exception, because my chart documents twelve months of pain and more than three months of provider-directed non-surgical care. I mention them only to show that the policy's three-month periods are the outer requirement and my records exceed them.

**4. Preoperative optimization.** The policy includes this note:

> "Note: It is incumbent on the surgeon to preoperatively optimize reasonably modifiable medical and behavioral health comorbidities."

My records document no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

**5. Other sections of the policy.** The policy also contains criteria addressed to other clinical situations, including:

> "Imaging shows a fracture of the femoral head or femoral neck."

> "Conservative management or surgical fixation is not considered a reasonable option."

> "Osteoarthritis, Avascular Necrosis (AVN), Inflammatory Arthritis"

I want to be straightforward about the limits of what I can quote: I have only excerpts of CMM-313, and the policy contains further conditions and lists that I do not have in front of me. Where I have not quoted the plan, I am arguing from my own records rather than from policy text. The denial notice told me that the request "does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity," but it did not identify which specific criterion was found unmet. Without that, I cannot know what evidence Cigna believes is missing.

## What I am asking for

I ask that Cigna overturn the denial and authorize total hip replacement, CPT 27130, as requested by Dr. Okafor. If Cigna upholds the denial in whole or in part, I ask that the plan identify in writing:

1. The specific criterion or criteria in Cigna CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026 that my request was found not to meet;
2. The specific records reviewed and the specific evidence Cigna considers missing; and
3. The credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination.

I also ask that my full prior authorization packet be re-reviewed, including the June 29, 2026 radiograph report, the physical therapy discharge note, and Dr. Okafor's operative recommendation. Please let me know if any additional records would help, and I will ask my surgeon's office to send them.

My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **February 17, 2027**. I am submitting this appeal through my plan's appeal process at my.cigna.com, using the appeal address and instructions printed on my denial letter; Cigna may also be reached at 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my member card.

Thank you for taking the time to review this again.

Sincerely,

**Morgan Ellison**
Member ID: W921829662
Reference number: POC-892F80BC2E-98290

[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

**Enclosures:** [List what you are sending — e.g., copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-21; radiograph report dated 2026-06-29; physical therapy discharge note; medication and injection records; surgeon's clinical notes and letter of medical necessity]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
```
